paragraphs.source_en: Whatever the justification for the Collection, hundreds of thousands of Albanians, Bosnians, Bulgarians, Croats, Greeks, Serbs, and others were made into recruits. In 1429, Murad II was presented with a treatise that boasted that ‘every year more or less fifty thousand male and female infidels are taken from the abode of war [enemy territory] as captives; those become Muslim, and their progeny join the rank of the faithful’.* A memoir written by a Serb Janissary who had served in the Ottoman military from 1456 to 1463 and had participated in the siege of Belgrade and an early sixteenth-century Ottoman document that served as a template for the levy both referred to the taking of children from one in every forty households.”

Apparently, they calculated that if their sons were to rise to grand vizier—the chief minister and advisor to the sultan, carrying out military and administrative duties—the family and village would be rewarded and protected.
